brief: The Market Ear compiles Goldman Sachs desk observations on last Thursday's record Nasdaq single-day market-cap loss and its aftermath. The shock drove the largest weekly L/S gross-leverage decline since Covid (to 207.5%, 26th percentile) and pushed net leverage to five-year lows, producing a momentum-factor crash severe enough that even a small bounce could be explosive. Goldman's panic vol index hit 9.57 on Thursday, above the 9.0 level Goldman's Garrett says has historically marked good buying opportunities, before closing the week at 9.2. A new Goldman metric, the Multiple Surprise Ratio, shows SPX recorded its largest volatility-adjusted surprise in 19 years last week (NDX top two, Russell 2000 top five on record), meaning options markets massively underpriced the moves. Despite a tech bounce and NDX reclaiming its trendline, tech volatility stays elevated. CTA trend-following signals have turned negative across ~60% of global equity markets including the S&P 500; Goldman's baseline sees $28bn of SPX futures selling this week and $45bn over the month, potentially pushing CTA positioning net short, with key levels at 7,685 and 7,550.
